To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) The production cross sections and momentum distributions of the residual nuclei have been measured for the first time in spallation induced by heavy ions on protons, and (ii) the data are in good agreement with predictions of statistical models, which are based on the concept of a composite target.

(a) the cross sections for the production of medium-mass residual products in 136Xe + p at 500 AMeV are systematically smaller by a factor of 1.6-2 than those in 136Xep + p at 1 AGeV; (b) the longitudinal momentum distributions of the medium-mass residual product are similar for both systems.
The production cross sections for the residual nuclei in reactions induced by 1 36Xe impinging on a proton at 500 AMeV have been determined.
